newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Mortgage Corp a solution to banks' exposure - HKMA.
newsitem.headline: Mortgage Corp a solution to banks' exposure - HKMA.

text.p: Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) deputy chief executive David Carse said on Thursday that Hong Kong's future Mortgage Corporation would offer a fundamental solution to banks' property lending exposure.

"I think the fundamental solution will be the Mortgage Corp," Carse said in response to reporters' questions on how the HKMA plans to deal with the problem of high mortgage loan exposure among Hong Kong banks.

Hong Kong's Mortgage Corp, which is expected to become operational in the fourth quarter of 1997, will offer banks the chance to sell some of their mortgages to the corporation, reducing the amount of mortgage loans on their books.
Carse said he did not rule out the possibility of applying tighter restrictions on banks' mortgage lending.
But he said he would prefer that banks practise voluntary restraint in lending.
"The ideal would be if banks were to exercise restraint themselves," he said.
Carse said that some banks already were practising self-restraint, but added it should be practised more widely.
